stories.title: Blood Cancer Nonprofit DKMS Takes 15K SF at 115 Broadway
stories.excerpt: DKMS, an international nonprofit fighting blood cancer and blood disorders, has signed a new office lease within Manhattan’s Financial District. The organization took 15,000 square feet across the 14th floor of 115 Broadway. The 22-story building makes up half of the Gothic-style Trinity Centre owned by Capital Properties and Madison International Realty. It is unclear whether the deal will relocate or expand DKMS from its currently listed offices at 40 Fulton Street, several blocks east in the Financial District’s Seaport area. A spokesperson for DKMS did not immediately respond to a request for comment. CBRE’s Laurence Briody represented DKMS in the transaction, while a Colliers team of Aidan Campbell, Michael Joseph and JP Howard negotiated on the behalf of the landlords. Meanwhile, at Trinity Centre’s neighboring 111 Broadway, MaryAnne Gilmartin’s MAG Partners secured a seventh-floor lease spanning 4,066 square feet. The September deal marked a relocation for Gilmartin’s firm from Global Holdings’ 1250 Broadway, according to a spokesperson. MAG Partners was represented by the Kaufman Organization’s Michael Kaufman. Lease terms and asking rents for either office deal were not disclosed, but Class B office rents in the Financial District averaged $51.91 per square foot in the third quarter of 2026, according to Colliers. The two fall arrivals at Trinity Centre are part of more than 100,000 square feet of leasing activity across 16 transactions recorded at the complex so far this year, according to a Colliers spokesperson. Work on the complex’s tenant amenity center was completed in August, and a collection of prebuilt office suites are on their way. Other fresh faces include advertiser LG Ad Solutions and Cook Law Firm at 115 Broadway, as well as consultancy company Perficient at 111 Broadway. Spokespeople for CBRE and the Kaufman Organization did not respond to requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: DKMS nonprofit leases 15K SF at 115 Broadway, Financial District Manhattan
Unclear if relocation from 40 Fulton Street or expansion of existing office
Trinity Centre ownership: Capital Properties & Madison International Realty
stories.summary: DKMS, an international blood cancer nonprofit, signed a 15,000-square-foot lease on the 14th floor of 115 Broadway in Manhattan's Financial District. The transaction was brokered by CBRE's Laurence Briody for the tenant and a Colliers team for the Gothic-style Trinity Centre landlords. It is unclear whether this represents a relocation from the organization's current 40 Fulton Street offices or an expansion.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. Office leasing activity in Lower Manhattan does not directly signal residential demand drivers or supply constraints affecting apartment development economics.

stories.title: NAI Hiffman Announces Lease at Arlington Heights Office Campus
stories.excerpt: NAI Hiffman represented a private ownership group in a 7,941-square-foot lease with Chicago Speech Therapy at 3436 N. Kennicott Avenue in Arlington Heights, Illinois. Chicago Speech Therapy, a provider of services for children with speech and language disorders, will open its newest location within the two-building office campus. The practice has multiple locations in Chicago and the northern suburbs, and selected the Arlington Heights property for its accessibility and convenience for families throughout the northwest suburbs. NAI Hiffman Executive Vice President Jason Wurtz, Associate Broker Sarah Walker and Associate Broker Bennett Baker represented the landlord in the transaction. “Chicago Speech Therapy’s long-term commitment reflects the tenant’s confidence in both the property and its location,” said Wurtz. “The campus offers the accessibility and flexibility that growing service-oriented tenants are looking for when making strategic real estate decisions.” The two-building office campus features updated common areas, ample parking and proximity to Endeavor Health Northwest Community Hospital and the Dundee Road retail corridor. bullets: Chicago Speech Therapy leases 7,941 SF at Arlington Heights office campus

stories.summary: Chicago Speech Therapy, a provider of speech and language disorder services for children, leased 7,941 square feet at 3436 N. Kennicott Avenue in Arlington Heights, Illinois, marking its newest location. NAI Hiffman represented the landlord in the transaction. The tenant cited the property's accessibility and convenience for families throughout the northwest suburbs as key drivers of the decision.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. A local service-provider lease signals modest local activity but does not indicate employment growth, population migration, or demand fundamentals affecting apartment development in the Chicago metro.

stories.title: Second Buyer Emerges for Vacant San Francisco Centre
stories.excerpt: A buyer has been found for the vacant San Francisco Centre, the San Francisco Chronicle first reported. Although the buyer has not been identified, reports on the Chronicle and the San Francisco Standard suggested that it could be New York-based Seven Equity Group, which specializes in repositioning distressed retail and mixed-use properties. The Seven Equity bid was selected from a pool of potential buyers after July’s collapse of a previous deal to acquire the 1.2-million-square-foot retail property. The Centre is now in the hands of a group of bondholders that previously purchased the debt position from lenders Deutsche Bank AG and JPMorgan Chase Bank, who originated a $558-million mortgage to Unibail-Rodamco-Westfield and Brookfield Properties in 2016, reported the Standard. URW and Brookfield defaulted on the debt last year, leading to foreclosure. Once a crown jewel of downtown San Francisco, the property is now believed to be valued at $130 million. The post Second Buyer Emerges for Vacant San Francisco Centre appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: San Francisco Centre (1.2M SF) second buyer emerges; Seven Equity Group likely purchaser
Property valued ~$130M post-foreclosure; previous deal collapsed July 2024
URW and Brookfield defaulted on $558M mortgage originated 2016; bondholders now control
stories.summary: A second buyer has emerged for the vacant 1.2-million-square-foot San Francisco Centre after a previous deal collapsed in July. Seven Equity Group, a New York-based firm specializing in repositioning distressed retail and mixed-use properties, is the likely purchaser. The property, now valued at approximately $130 million, was foreclosed after URW and Brookfield Properties defaulted on a $558 million mortgage; bondholders currently hold the asset.
stories.impact: Signals distressed mixed-use asset repositioning in San Francisco's downtown core, but mixed-use retail recovery does not directly drive multifamily fundamentals. However, successful retail repositioning could stabilize downtown foot traffic and support demand for nearby residential in SOMA and Mission Bay if it attracts office tenants or foot traffic.

stories.title: The Boulder Group Arranges Sale of Net Leased Steak ’n Shake in Aurora
stories.excerpt: The Boulder Group completed the sale of a single-tenant net-leased restaurant property occupied by Steak ’n Shake in Aurora, Illinois, for $1.27 million. The property is located at 4333 Fox Valley Center Drive, near the intersection of Illinois Route 59 and New York Street. The property sits across from Fox Valley Mall, a roughly 1,500,000-square-foot regional shopping center anchored by Macy’s and JCPenney. Nearby national retailers include Costco, Whole Foods Market, The Home Depot, Menards and Meijer. Randy Blankstein, Jimmy Goodman and John Feeney of The Boulder Group represented both parties in the transaction. The seller was an investment group that had held the property as part of a net lease portfolio. The buyer was a local investor acquiring the property as a net-leased investment. “Investor appetite for net leased restaurant properties along established retail corridors has remained steady, even with interest rates holding higher for longer,” said Blankstein. The post The Boulder Group Arranges Sale of Net Leased Steak ’n Shake in Aurora appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Steak 'n Shake net-lease property in Aurora, Illinois sold for $1.27M
Location: 4333 Fox Valley Center Drive, near IL Route 59 and New York Street
Buyer: local investor; seller: investment group divesting net-lease portfolio
stories.summary: The Boulder Group arranged the sale of a single-tenant net-leased Steak 'n Shake restaurant at 4333 Fox Valley Center Drive in Aurora, Illinois, for $1.27 million. The property sits across from Fox Valley Mall, a 1.5-million-square-foot regional shopping center anchored by Macy's and JCPenney, with nearby national retailers including Costco, Whole Foods, The Home Depot, Menards, and Meijer. A local investor purchased the property from an investment group divesting its net-lease portfolio.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. Single-tenant net-lease restaurant sales do not signal demand or supply shifts affecting apartment markets; this transaction reflects investor appetite for stable, lower-risk retail income but does not indicate residential market dynamics in the Chicago metro.

stories.title: Alexandria Divesting Part of Fenway Megacampus to Institutional User
stories.excerpt: Alexandria Real Estate Equities disclosed in an earnings report that it has entered into a purchase and sale agreement with an institutional user for the sale of 421 Park Dr. on the Alexandria Center for Life Science – Fenway Megacampus in Boston. The disposition of the office and lab building is expected to generate significant sales proceeds and to reduce future potential construction spend by approximately $136 million, with closing anticipated later in the fourth quarter. The news comes after the announcement by tech incubator MassChallenge that it would move its global headquarters into 401 Park Dr., also part of the Fenway Megacampus. Alexandria paid $1.5 billion to Samuels & Associates in 2021 to acquire a block containing 401 Park, 421 Park and 201 Brookline. Although Alexandria sold part of 421 Park to Boston Children’s Hospital for $173 million in 2023, the hospital said last year it was pausing its plans to move into the 268,000 square feet it acquired, citing budget constraints, according to the Boston Business Journal The post Alexandria Divesting Part of Fenway Megacampus to Institutional User appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Alexandria Real Estate selling 421 Park Dr, Boston Fenway Megacampus to institutional user
Sale reduces future construction spend by ~$136M; closing expected Q4 2024
MassChallenge relocating HQ to 401 Park Dr; Boston Children's Hospital paused 268K SF move citing budget constraints (2024)
stories.summary: Alexandria Real Estate Equities announced a purchase and sale agreement to sell 421 Park Drive, an office and lab building on its Alexandria Center for Life Science–Fenway Megacampus in Boston, to an institutional user. The disposition is expected to generate significant proceeds and reduce future construction spending by approximately $136 million, with closing anticipated in Q4. The news follows MassChallenge's announcement that it would move its global headquarters into 401 Park Drive on the same campus; Boston Children's Hospital, which acquired part of 421 Park for $173 million in 2023, paused its move citing budget constraints.
stories.impact: Alexandria's need to divest and curtail construction on a flagship life-science megacampus signals softening demand and financing pressure in the Boston biotech/lab market, potentially freeing up institutional capital for multifamily acquisitions. Paused occupancy by Boston Children's reflects budget-constrained institutional demand; mixed-use campuses competing with residential for capital in Boston's tight real estate market.

stories.title: Essex Realty Group Closes 12-Unit Rogers Park Multifamily Transaction
stories.excerpt: Essex Realty Group announced the sale of 1706–1716 W. Farwell Avenue, a 12-unit multifamily apartment building in Chicago’s Rogers Park neighborhood. Essex Realty Group Principals Doug Imber, Kate Varde, and Managing Director Rick Ofman represented the seller, while Essex Principal Jim Darrow represented the purchaser, a California-based 1031 exchange investor. The property underwent a complete renovation in 2013 and features eight two-bedroom apartments and four three-bedroom duplex apartments. Unit amenities include hardwood floors, granite countertops, stainless steel appliances and in-unit laundry. “The 1706 Farwell transaction reflects the continued strength of the neighborhood’s appeal to investors,” said Ofman. Located in Chicago’s Rogers Park neighborhood, 1706–1716 W. Farwell Avenue benefits from convenient access to public transportation, including the Rogers Park Metra station and the Morse CTA Red Line station. The property is also approximately 1.2 miles north of Loyola University Chicago and within walking distance of the dining and retail corridors. bullets: Essex Realty closes 12-unit Rogers Park multifamily sale; buyer: California 1031 exchange investor
Property: 1706–1716 W. Farwell Avenue, 8 two-bed and 4 three-bed duplex units

stories.summary: Essex Realty Group announced the sale of 1706–1716 W. The property underwent complete renovation in 2013 and features eight two-bedroom apartments and four three-bedroom duplex units with hardwood floors, granite countertops, stainless steel appliances, and in-unit laundry. stories.title: Alexandria Reports Improved Sales and Leasing Amid Financial Hardships
stories.excerpt: Leasing has picked up steam for Alexandria Real Estate Equities, but the real estate investment trust continues to struggle with financial hemorrhaging. The REIT, which invests heavily in laboratories and life sciences facilities, reported a net loss of $638.5 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same period last year when it lost $234.9 million, according to executives who spoke during Alexandria’s Tuesday earnings call. Funds from operations (FFO) landed at $264.4 million in the last quarter in contrast to the $296 million in the second quarter and $377.8 million year-over-year. Third-quarter revenue closed at $671 million compared to $662.7 million at the end of the second quarter but declined from $751.9 million in the third quarter of 2025. “Despite the current challenges in the life science real estate market, we continue to benefit from a high-quality tenant base with 57 percent of our annual rental revenue coming from the investment-grade or publicly traded large-cap tenants,” Joel Marcus, Alexandria’s executive chairman and founder, said during the call. Some items in its portfolio are in contract to sell, such as 421 Park Drive of the Alexandria Center for Life Science – Fenway Megacampus in Boston for about $136 million. The potential buyer for that deal was not disclosed. Alexandria sold $234 million in assets in the third quarter. Alexandria recorded 87.1 percent occupancy across its operating properties as leasing numbers have picked up, in the third quarter in particular. The REIT leased 1.2 million square feet of space in the three months ending Sept. 30, which exceeded 979,822 square feet signed on average in the six preceding quarters. The company will still face significant challenges in 2027, when up to 1.4 million square feet of leases will expire, and with it an estimated $100.5 million of annual rental revenue. bullets: Alexandria Q3 2024 net loss $638.5M vs. $234.9M prior year; FFO $264.4M down from $377.8M YoY
Revenue declined to $671M Q3 2024 vs. $751.9M Q3 2023; 57% of annual rental revenue from investment-grade tenants

stories.impact: Alexandria's severe financial deterioration and FFO compression signal a funding crisis in the life-sciences REIT sector, forcing asset sales and construction pullbacks. Capital flight from lab/life-science is redirecting institutional investor appetite to alternative asset classes, including multifamily, and may reduce competition for residential debt and equity in key markets like Boston and San Diego.

stories.title: NBA Store Seeks New, Larger Location Up to 25K Square Feet
stories.excerpt: Jump ball. The NBA Store, which is operated by Fanatics-owned sports apparel company Lids, is planning to relocate from its longtime retail location at 545 Fifth Avenue into a larger space, Commercial Observer can first report. The retailer of team jerseys, collectibles and other basketball-related merchandise is exploring seven potential locations around Midtown Manhattan to expand from its current 15,000 square feet of sellable retail space that it has leased since 2015 at the corner of 45th Street and Fifth Avenue, a source familiar with the move told CO. Lids, which is leading the leasing process, is targeting 20,000 to 25,000 square feet of sellable space for the new store and is eyeing properties around Midtown, including in Times Square, along with several vacant buildings on Fifth Avenue, according to the source. The NBA Store lease is up at the Moinian Group-owned 545 Fifth Avenue in 2031, but the retailer is looking to have a new site lined up in about a year to have sufficient time to organize the build-out, the source said. Lids is looking to expand with a bigger “and more inviting ground floor” in the midst of a record year for the NBA Store, where business was bolstered this year by the New York Knicks capturing their first NBA title since 1973. In addition to adding space to sell jerseys and merchandise, the store’s operators hope to design an enhanced entrance. The NBA Store first launched in 1998 at 666 Fifth Avenue before setting up a smaller temporary store at 590 Fifth Avenue from 2011 to 2015, prior to relocating to 545 Fifth. The Moinian Group did not immediately return a request for comment. Fanatics declined to comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: NBA Store seeking 20K–25K SF in Midtown Manhattan; current lease (15K SF) expires 2031 at 545 Fifth Avenue
Lids-operated retailer exploring 7 locations: Times Square, Fifth Avenue vacant buildings, Midtown corridor
Retailer wants new site within ~1 year to organize build-out before 2031 lease expiration
stories.summary: The NBA Store, operated by Fanatics-owned Lids, is planning to relocate from its longtime 15,000-square-foot retail space at 545 Fifth Avenue (corner of 45th and Fifth) to a larger location of 20,000–25,000 square feet in Midtown Manhattan. Although the current lease does not expire until 2031, the retailer is exploring seven potential sites around Midtown—including Times Square and vacant Fifth Avenue buildings—and aims to secure a new location within approximately one year to allow time for buildout.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily. Retail expansion signals confidence in Midtown foot traffic and commercial leasing recovery, but does not drive residential demand or indicate population migration or employment growth affecting apartment supply/demand in Manhattan submarkets.

stories.title: Shorenstein Buys Fully Leased SoHo Office Property From Tishman Speyer
stories.excerpt: Tishman Speyer has sold the 12-story, 155,000-square-foot office building at 148 Lafayette Street in SoHo, at the corner of Lafayette and Howard streets, to Shorenstein Properties for $132.5 million, or $866 per square foot, according to Tishman. The deal was repped by Newmark‘s Adam Spies, Doug Harmon, Adam Doneger, Marcella Fasulo, Avery Silverstein and Joshua King. Shorenstein outbid several institutional bidders, including private equity funds, for the building, according to a source with knowledge of the deal. The Real Deal was first to report the sale. Tishman is selling the property on a quick turnaround at a sizable profit, having purchased the building from Epic in May 2025 for $105.5 million, with $68.3 million of that coming in the form of an acquisition loan from Blackstone Real Estate Debt Strategies. Prior to the 2025 purchase, Tishman had not bought an office building anywhere in the U.S. since 2021, and had not purchased an office building in Manhattan since 2019, according to previous reporting in Commercial Observer. The $105.5 million purchase price in 2025 represented a decline from the $126.5 million Epic paid for the building in 2012. “We acquired 148 Lafayette with a clear plan and executed it ahead of schedule, generating an attractive return for our investors,” Chris Shehadeh, senior managing director at Tishman, said in a statement. “This successful outcome reaffirms our conviction in the continued demand for premier office assets in prime Manhattan neighborhoods to both companies seeking exceptional work environments and institutional investors targeting high-quality real estate.” The building contains 141,359 square feet of office space, which is 100 percent leased to tenants including investment firm General Catalyst, artificial intelligence code review firm Graphite, coworking firm WeWork, cosmetics company Charlotte Tilbury, digital picture frame company Aura Frames and consulting firm Keystone. Tishman purchased May 2025 for $105.5M (68% financed via Blackstone debt); resale 7 months later at 26% markup

Tishman had purchased the building from Epic in May 2025 for $105.5 million (with $68.3 million financed by Blackstone Real Estate Debt Strategies), marking a 26 percent profit on a seven-month hold. Shorenstein outbid several institutional and private equity bidders.
stories.impact: Tishman's quick flip and Shorenstein's aggressive bidding signal renewed institutional appetite for fully-leased Manhattan office, but do not directly affect multifamily development. However, the sale validates SoHo's office desirability and occupancy stability, supporting mixed-use and conversion scenarios; Blackstone's debt deployment suggests capital flowing toward opportunistic office rather than multifamily development.

stories.title: Welltower Earnings Boosted by Senior Housing Acquisitions
stories.excerpt: Welltower, the country’s largest senior housing landlord, reported another strong quarter with increased pricing power and ample acquisitions. During its third-quarter earnings call on Tuesday morning, the Ohio-based real estate investment trust (REIT) reported its profits were up 24.6 percent per share year-over-year, with occupancy throughout its portfolio at 88 percent. Welltower continues to buy properties at a healthy clip, while it executes a long-term move to offload a significant slice of its outpatient medical properties. Welltower’s normalized funds from operations (FFO) were $1.67 per share, up 24.6 percent annually. This company figure excludes line items like debt payments, transactions costs and legal fees. The REIT’s revenue totaled $3.7 billion between July and September, up roughly 38 percent from $2.7 billion over the same three-month period in 2025. Instead of large-scale mergers and acquisitions — which Shankh Mitra, CEO of Welltower, said they “avoid like the plague” — the REIT has completed 196 different transactions this year, with $21 billion in investments completed or under contract so far. Within the third quarter, Welltower acquired 43 senior housing properties for $2.7 billion. Despite this activity, Mitra told investors that it acquires less than 3 percent of the assets it screens. Welltower is primed to buy on distress, said Nikhil Chaudhri, co-president and chief investment officer of Welltower, noting the roughly $8 billion of U.S. senior housing debt due in 2026. “While some owners may recapitalize, most will sell as the impact of rising rates offsets improved industry fundamentals,” Chaudhri said. “That is where Welltower comes in.” Welltower has offloaded $2.1 billion worth of outpatient medical assets so far this year, including 25 properties within the quarter. Sales weren’t exclusive to medical offices, however. Earlier this month, Brookdale Senior Living announced it acquired 30 communities leased from Welltower for $290 milli
bullets: Welltower Q3 2024 FFO $1.67/share, up 24.6% YoY; occupancy 88% across senior housing portfolio
Revenue $3.7B Q3 2024, up 38% YoY; 196 acquisitions completed in 2024 with $21B deployed
REIT divesting outpatient medical properties while scaling senior housing acquisitions; strong pricing power reported
stories.summary: Welltower, the nation's largest senior housing landlord, reported strong Q3 2024 results with FFO up 24.6 percent year-over-year to $1.67 per share and portfolio occupancy at 88 percent. Revenue totaled $3.7 billion in Q3 2024, up 38 percent from $2.7 billion in Q3 2023. The REIT completed 196 acquisitions totaling $21 billion in 2024 while executing a long-term strategy to offload outpatient medical properties, demonstrating robust pricing power.
stories.impact: Welltower's aggressive capital deployment in senior housing (1,000+ basis points FFO growth, 196 deals annually) and pricing power signal strong demand tailwinds in aging demographics, but compete with multifamily for institutional capital and debt capacity. Senior housing's superior occupancy (88%) and cash-flow stability are attracting REITs away from multifamily; rising senior-housing valuations and debt availability may compress multifamily pricing and financing availability in gateway and secondary markets.
